ideas: How bad experiences help us survive and avoid danger
Whether some good memories last just as long

phrases.meaning: be remembered for a long time
affect someone for a long time

phrases.phrase: go over it again and again

model: I'd say the main reason is that our brains are designed to protect us. Bad experiences are basically warnings, so they stick in our minds because remembering them helps us avoid the same danger next time. It's a kind of survival instinct. For example, when I was a teenager, I was riding my bike home in the rain when I skidded and fell on a busy road. I wasn't badly hurt, but I still remember every detail, and after that, I was on high alert whenever it rained. On the other hand, I can hardly remember what I did on most good days that year. Another reason is that we tend to go over negative events again and again, asking ourselves what went wrong, and that repetition makes the memory stronger. Good experiences often feel normal, so we take them for granted. That said, I don't think it's always true. Really big happy moments, like a wedding or graduation, can leave a lasting impression too. But generally, small pleasures fade over time much faster than things we learned the hard way.
